# Signet

> Your contracts are audited. Your website isn't. Signet protects what your users actually load: no single hacked key can change a dApp's site (CI only proposes; approvers approve; TapeOut circuit #6 decides, with a timelock nobody can bypass), a watchtower checks what the site serves, it can freeze instantly, and users with Signet Guard can't sign anything the team didn't approve: Guard blocks the signature. Signet builds on TapeKit's on-chain file verification and adds the signing-time allowlist (circuit #7), risk-tiered approvals with timelocks decided by circuit #6, CI that can only propose, a domain proof, and a verified copy read from X Layer (built; live with Pro).
>
> Signet lets a dApp team seal each release of its website on X Layer (file hashes, the contracts and spenders the site may ask a wallet to sign for, the outside origins it may use). A TapeOut circuit decides when a release goes live (CI can propose and publish but never approve; humans approve; risky changes wait 24 h). Users who run the Guard browser extension have every page and every signature checked against the sealed release; the signing decision comes from a second TapeOut circuit. Users without Guard are NOT protected at signing; a watchtower alerts the team instead.

Status (2026-11-24): live on X Layer mainnet (chain 196) since 2026-11-18 (docs/mainnet.md):
- Release-policy circuit #6 and Guard decision circuit #7 on TapeOut processor #101 (0x73153e5fd2Acac604D49d6ca9fea27b750718F22), each verified on all 512 inputs on two RPCs.
- SignetRegistry 0x98dB5B6B1545D0fb374da40a02045B93398E0589, SignetFactory 0xc5e12ffe9D5bE7085441bD955724A6FAff9f7986, ReleaseGate implementation 0xD14697C1dFEAdA3A117Ff8CD5358c80743453B3D.
- Signet's site gate 0xa3d4dfb5fB47D2CcF9b4a0a0fcC64Ac3fFef4503 (signetguard.xyz): releases #3, #4 and #5 published 2026-11-20, #6 was the tier-11 guardian change, #7, #8 and #9 published 2026-11-24 (#8's files are also stored in TapeOut's SiteRegistry, circuit #5's container). Observe mode.
- misthos.world gate 0xDfFf2307d45df1995502d8b300aE9AfbB01c4a59: the team's own app (on Arc, not an outside adopter), sealed in server-rendered mode; release 1 proposed by its CI and approved 2026-11-24, publishable from 2026-11-25. Observe mode.
- `pnpm verify:claims`: every claim checked on mainnet or in the repo (claims.json).
- Site (landing, dashboard, /prove against mainnet, no wallet): https://signetguard.xyz (Cloudflare Pages).
- CLI: `signetguard` on npm (0.2.2). Guard: a signed pre-release zip on GitHub (0.3.2), not in the Chrome Web Store yet; its privacy policy: https://signetguard.xyz/privacy.
- Not live: enforce mode on any mainnet gate, the gateway (staging only). The watchtower runs for signetguard.xyz on GitHub Actions' schedule (every 4–12 hours in practice) and publishes its status and its last /prove run; Telegram alerts to the team's chat are set up (a test alert was accepted by Telegram on 2026-11-20, watchtower run 44746304914).

## Built on TapeOut (what is really used)
- Two TapeOut circuits on processor #101: #6 decides when a release may publish (ReleaseGate calls it on every publish and unfreeze; a Solidity copy of the same gates decides only if that call fails or returns a malformed answer, with an on-chain event; the circuit's beacon has no owner, so the rule can't be upgraded); #7 decides Guard's allow/warn/block at signing.
- The Circuit Container of circuit #5 (0x8E2E14Ac2B8EfAB942d2dAEbe232071460bA94Ed, opened) + TapeOut's SiteRegistry (0xd6EFb7adCc9c83dC4924Ad56f6a8E4e969b9ADB6, the storage behind DeWEB) hold each release's sealed manifest (and, once Pro is live, the files of the verified copy); SignetRegistry writes only files an approved release lists, as the container's 30-day SiteRegistry operator.
- Files over 48,000 bytes are stored in 24,000-byte pieces, one proved piece per transaction (SignetRegistry.writeChunk on top of SiteRegistry.appendChunk).
- Reading and checking follow TapeKit / TAP-10: every file's size and SHA-256 checked against the chain, two independent RPCs that must agree; the gateway reuses TapeKit's service-worker design.

## Roadmap (planned, not built)
- TapeSend alerts from the watchtower to a team's container inbox (about 0.0000039 OKB per alert). Waiting on TapeOut to confirm the DeWEB hub implementation upgraded on 2026-11-18 (docs/ecosystem-integration.md).
- TapeCode sealing: TapeCode uploads to a staging container, `signet seal --from-container` reads it from the chain, and the approved release is copied to production (design ready, docs/ecosystem-integration.md).
- Hosting the site itself on DeWEB (about 0.0044 OKB of storage); the Chrome Web Store listing; watchtower in 3 regions.
